provider: git-annex rclone special remote (built into annex since 2023)

free_tier.stated: N/A. Front-end to rclone storage backends, inheriting free tiers of supported providers. Documentation lists Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Mega, pCloud, Box, Yandex, Jottacloud, WebDAV, FTP, SFTP, Swift, B2, and S3.

egress.terms: Determined by the selected rclone backend. Rclone handles throttling and retries across remote endpoints.

tooling: Two paths: (a) `git annex initremote type=rclone ..`. Native, no extra install, documented via `rclone gitannex -h`; (b) the older `git-annex-remote-rclone` bash script (DanielDent, ~300 lines). rclone itself is a single static binary.
chaining: Combines git-annex versioning, checksum verification, and partial checkouts with rclone remote storage backends. A single repository can configure multiple rclone remotes across diverse storage providers using git annex copy commands.
limits_note: Per-backend: file size caps, per-day upload quotas, API rate limits all apply unchanged. rclone's Drive backend has its own 750 GB/day upload cap; OneDrive throttles. Encrypted annex remotes lose rclone's server-side dedupe.
reliability_note: Solid; the native remote removed the bash-script dependency. The failure mode is per-backend token expiry and drive-level rate limiting, which rclone surfaces as retries rather than data loss.

evidence.proved: 'With a recent version of rclone and git-annex, it is not necessary to install anything else, just use `git-annex initremote type=rclone ...`'
the gitannex bridge command exists in rclone proper
backend feature matrix (Internet Archive, Drive, OneDrive, Box, Mega, WebDAV, SFTP, S3 all Tier 1-3 with R/W)
